domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification to lowest terms

skills.name: Prepare operands for subtraction
skills.definition: Put quantities into a subtraction-ready form by matching denominators when needed and/or rewriting whole numbers or mixed numbers into compatible whole-plus-fraction form before subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: Inherited from the K=5 aggregation: both skills are preparatory transformations that make subtraction possible.

skills.name: Execute subtraction and regroup if needed
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction of aligned whole and fraction parts, including borrowing/regrouping one whole into denominator-sized fractional units when necessary to complete the subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: S04 is a conditional extension of S03 during execution: regrouping only occurs when ordinary aligned subtraction reveals that the fractional part is too small. In practice, these two skills form a single execution phase, and S04 has a prerequisite relationship to subtraction work. At K=4, merging them preserves a meaningful distinction between preparation, execution, and finalization.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or simplify zero fractional parts to a simpler whole-number form.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification remains diagnostically useful and often produces different student errors than answer composition.

skills.name: Compose final answer
skills.definition: Present the result in final acceptable form by combining whole and fractional parts or expressing the answer as a fraction, mixed number, or integer.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final presentation is still distinguishable from simplification; some items end with direct presentation while others require explicit reduction first.
